answer: One concrete defense is staking a deposit that is locked for a long period and slashed if the account misbehaves. A single person can still open many accounts, but each one ties up real capital, so the cost of a fake army grows linearly with its size. Think of a narrow inlet that admits only one boat at a time: throughput stays low even when the sea is crowded. Like crystal forming slowly in a karst cave, reputation should accrete over time through verified work, so an attacker must pay both money and time for every identity they create.
